title: CI: daily super run failed
thread:
**Issue #4375 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4375: CI: daily super run failed
Opened by @github-actions[bot].

[super run 44847881026](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/44847881026) on `_staging` (`d5f68be`, workflow_dispatch) failed:

| Job | Result |
|---|---|
| [daily tests (cargo test -- --ignored)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/44847881026/job/136671957847) | cancelled |
| [e2e (3/8)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/44847881026/job/136674669592) | failure |

Each link opens that job's log. This issue stays open while the run is red and the next run that passes every job closes it. `gh workflow run super.yml --ref <branch>` runs it again on demand.

Night bot: this run is on `_staging`, so it is yours, and it comes first (`priority:high`, and you take it before every other queued item): production promotes itself only from a daily run on `_staging` that passes every job, so it waits on this fix, and `_staging` holds still until this issue closes (scripts/promote-staging.sh, the freeze). Fix every failed job here, in the one pull request on `main` that closes this: when it closes, `_staging` takes main's first green commit after the close and the super run starts on it at once, and a run still red opens a new issue. Before you start, look for an open pull request or issue already fixing one of these jobs, and build on it instead of fixing the same test twice. Root-cause each failed job from its log and fix it in a pull request: a flake is not a root cause, so make a flaky test robust instead of re-running it, and never skip, disable or quarantine a test to get green. Reproduce it with the job's own command (CLAUDE.md, Commands; one fuzz seed is `cargo jackioh fuzz --from <seed> --seeds 1`, with `--handicap` for the handicapped wave and `--duos` for the Duos wave; a daily test is `cargo test -p <crate> <name> -- --ignored`). A pull request's CI runs only the e2e smoke specs and leaves the tests marked `#[ignore = "daily: …"]` out, so say in the pull request which job here the fix makes pass and how you checked it. You cannot change `.github/`: make the part of the fix that lives elsewhere, and when the rest needs a workflow or an action, give the exact lines to change there and ask a person to make them.

---
_Posted by `.github/workflows/super.yml`._
```

handoff.draft:
**Human required:** in `.github/workflows/super.yml`, split the `daily-tests` job into the three-leg matrix given in Steps 1–2 (the bot may not change `.github/`). Also read the log of `e2e (3/8)` (job 136674669592), which did not reproduce locally, and name the test that failed (Open questions).

## Goal

Make both red jobs of super run 44847881026 (`_staging` at `d5f68be`) pass on the next run on `_staging`. No CI log was readable from here, so I reproduced each job with its own command on this branch's base, `e41f3eb` (`d5f68be` plus six commits).

- **`daily tests (cargo test -- --ignored)`, cancelled.** The job hit its `timeout-minutes: 60`. It runs every `#[ignore = "daily: …"]` test as one `cargo test`, one test binary after another.
  - #4249 (`968d1cbde6`, 2026-11-20 05:04) grew the pool probe (`crates/tools/tests/pool_probe.rs`): besides the cards' suite, it now builds and runs the AI's, the server's and the tools' suites under `jackioh-engine/pool-probe`. That build is a nested `cargo test` in a separate, cold `target/pool-probe`.
  - The previous super run (#4318) predates #4249, and its daily tests passed.
  - Local times on a 4-core GitHub runner, test execution only, compile time not counted:

    | Test binary | Time |
    |---|---|
    | `ai_slow` | 874 s |
    | tools `jackioh` bin | 1024 s |
    | `jackioh_run` lib (`map_fuzz_daily_wide_sweep`, added after `d5f68be`) | 406 s |
    | server `actor::perf` | 64 s |
    | tools `perf.rs` | 18 s |
    | pool probe | over 1,320 s (its nested cold build alone took 581 s) |

  - That is over an hour of tests before the workspace compiles. No test failed.
  - The fix is structural, as super.yml already does for fuzz, gates and e2e: three parallel legs that together run each ignored test exactly once, each well under 60 minutes. No test is removed or weakened, and no timeout is raised.
- **`e2e (3/8)`, failure. Not reproduced.**
  - I ran the shard (specs 09, 10, 20, 31, 32, 43, 46, 54) twice as `.github/actions/e2e-shard` does: release `jackioh-server` and `jackioh`, a `build:e2e` client, Chrome 157.
  - Once idle (8:23) and once under the daily tests' full CPU load (13:17), 227 of 227 tests passed both times. That includes spec 46's new tab-row check (#4340) at all seven sizes.
  - Nothing changes for it here; see Open questions.

## Files to touch

| Path | | What |
|---|---|---|
| `.github/workflows/super.yml` | change | header line for `daily tests` (lines 10–11); the `daily-tests` job (lines 297–316) becomes a three-leg matrix |

Leave alone:
- every test and `#[ignore]` reason;
- `report`'s `needs:` (the matrix keeps the key `daily-tests`);
- `bot/go/tests/cigate_test.go`: it counts super.yml's first jobs by key and expects 6. One matrix job under `daily-tests` keeps it at 6, and the job keeps its `environment:` line.

Governing rules: CLAUDE.md, "CI" (daily tests); `crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs`'s rule that every ignore reads `daily: …`; #4181 and #4249 (the pool probe).

## Steps

1. **super.yml header, lines 10–11.** Replace them with:
   ```yaml
   #   daily tests     every Rust test `#[ignore = "daily: …"]` leaves out of a pull request's cargo test:
   #                   the many-game sweeps, whose rule a cheaper test holds per pull request, in three
   #                   legs: every crate but the tools, the tools, and the tools' pool probe (#4375)
   ```
2. **super.yml, the `daily-tests` job.** Replace the comment above `daily-tests:` and the whole job, through its `cargo test` line, with this block. It follows the `db` job's `include:` matrix and ci.yml's `# shellcheck disable=SC2086` pattern.
   ```yaml
     # The Rust tests too slow or too statistical for every pull request: each `#[ignore = "daily: …"]`
     # in the workspace, its reason naming what holds the same rule per pull request (acceptance.rs
     # holds every ignore to that form), and nothing else. `--tests` leaves out the doc-tests, whose
     # `ignore` blocks are not tests at all. Three legs that together run each ignored test once
     # (#4375): as one job they ran past its 60 minutes once the pool probe took the AI's, the server's
     # and the tools' suites too (#4249). The tools leg leaves the probe's four tests to their own leg.
     # That leg builds only jackioh-tools, which does not depend on the server, so it fetches every
     # crate first for the probe's nested `cargo test --offline` builds.
     daily-tests:
       name: daily tests (${{ matrix.leg }})
       if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
       environment: ${{ vars.CI_GATE_ENVIRONMENT || '' }}
       runs-on: ubuntu-latest
       timeout-minutes: 60
       strategy:
         fail-fast: false
         matrix:
           include:
             - leg: every crate but the tools
               key: crates
               targets: "--workspace --exclude jackioh-tools --tests"
               skip: ""
             - leg: tools
               key: tools
               targets: "-p jackioh-tools --tests"
               skip: "--skip _passes_with_every_random_pool_rotated"
             - leg: pool probe
               key: pool-probe
               targets: "-p jackioh-tools --test pool_probe"
               skip: ""
       env:
         CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG: "0"
       steps:
         - uses: actions/checkout@v4
         - uses: ./.github/actions/setup
           with:
             node: "false"
             cache-key: daily-tests-${{ matrix.key }}
         - name: every crate in Cargo.lock, for the probe's offline builds
           if: ${{ matrix.key == 'pool-probe' }}
           run: cargo fetch
         - name: this leg's tests a pull request leaves to the daily run
           env:
             TARGETS: ${{ matrix.targets }}
             SKIP: ${{ matrix.skip }}
           run: |
             # shellcheck disable=SC2086 # TARGETS and SKIP are several arguments on purpose.
             cargo test $TARGETS --features jackioh-engine/testkit,jackioh-engine/ts -- --ignored $SKIP
   ```
   Why each leg holds:
   - `_passes_with_every_random_pool_rotated` matches exactly the four probe tests (`every_{cards,ai,server,tools}_test_passes_with_every_random_pool_rotated`) and no other test name.
   - `--test pool_probe` without `--tests` runs only that binary.
   - `--exclude jackioh-tools` leaves every other member to the first leg.

## Tests

Run from the repository root:
- `docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/repo" --workdir /repo rhysd/actionlint:1.7.7 -color .github/workflows/super.yml` passes.
- `cd bot/go && go test ./...` passes; `TestWorkflows_CIAndTheSuperRunWaitForTheRunnerGate` still counts 6 first jobs.
- Optional coverage proof. Each list is the leg's own command with `--list --format terse` added after `--ignored`:
  - `cargo test --workspace --tests --features jackioh-engine/testkit,jackioh-engine/ts -- --ignored --list --format terse | sort > all.txt`
  - The same for each of the three legs (the tools leg with its `--skip`), concatenated, `sort`ed, then `diff`ed against `all.txt`. The diff must be empty.
- `gh workflow run super.yml --ref <the branch>`. All three `daily tests (…)` legs must be green and each under 60 minutes.

## Done when

- [ ] super.yml's header and `daily-tests` job read as in Steps 1–2.
- [ ] actionlint and `go test ./...` in `bot/go` pass.
- [ ] A dispatched super run on the branch shows `daily tests (every crate but the tools)`, `daily tests (tools)` and `daily tests (pool probe)` green, each under 60 minutes.
- [ ] `e2e (3/8)`: its log was read. Its failing test is named in the pull request, with an issue opened for it if it fails again.
- [ ] The pull request on `main` says which job each change makes pass and closes #4375.

## Risks

- **Coverage.** A leg selection that drops or repeats a test. The legs follow cargo's own package and target selection, and the optional list diff proves it.
- **Offline probe.** Without `cargo fetch`, the probe's nested `cargo test -p jackioh-server --offline` finds the server's crates missing on a fresh runner. The original single job fetched them through `--workspace`.
- **Cold caches.**
  - Each leg has its own `cache-key` (the setup action asks a matrix for that).
  - The first run of each key compiles from scratch, the probe's nested `target/pool-probe` included (about 10 minutes here).
  - Locally, every leg's tests plus a full compile stay well under 60 minutes: about 23, 18 and 25 minutes of tests.
- **Growth.**
  - When `FUZZ_POOL` passes 799 cards, `the_days_extra_seeds_keep_every_pool_card_s_deals_as_the_pool_grows` adds up to about 15 minutes to the tools leg (`DAILY_TOP_UP_MAX`, `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs`). That is still under 60.
  - A future slow test goes in whichever leg owns its crate.
- **Runner cost.** Three runners instead of one. The runner gate counts runs, not jobs.

## Open questions

- **`e2e (3/8)`: which test failed?** Only its log says, and neither the planner nor the bot can read it. Both local runs passed every test at `e41f3eb`.
  - Since `d5f68be`, main gained R4250000 (`c4bc8bd2a8`): a match or co-op socket's reconnect backoff starts over on its first view, not on open.
  - That was the one client change, and it is a candidate if the failure was a networked spec (20, 54, or 46's signed-in screens) meeting 429s.
  - If the log names a test that fails on its own assertion, it needs its own issue with that name.
- **Alternative rejected:** raising `timeout-minutes` to about 120. The work is serial and only grows with every new daily test, while the legs run in parallel and each keeps the 60-minute budget. A person may still prefer it.

````markdown
               targets: "-p jackioh-tools --tests"
               skip: "--skip _passes_with_every_random_pool_rotated"
             - leg: pool probe
               key: pool-probe
               targets: "-p jackioh-tools --test pool_probe"
               skip: ""
       env:
         CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG: "0"
       steps:
         - uses: actions/checkout@v4
         - uses: ./.github/actions/setup
           with:
             node: "false"
             cache-key: daily-tests-${{ matrix.key }}
         - name: every crate in Cargo.lock, for the probe's offline builds
           if: ${{ matrix.key == 'pool-probe' }}
           run: cargo fetch
         - name: this leg's tests a pull request leaves to the daily run
           env:
             TARGETS: ${{ matrix.targets }}
             SKIP: ${{ matrix.skip }}
           run: |
             # shellcheck disable=SC2086 # TARGETS and SKIP are several arguments on purpose.
             cargo test $TARGETS --features jackioh-engine/testkit,jackioh-engine/ts -- --ignored $SKIP
   ```
   Why each leg holds:
   - `_passes_with_every_random_pool_rotated` matches exactly the four probe tests (`every_{cards,ai,server,tools}_test_passes_with_every_random_pool_rotated`) and no other test name.
   - `--test pool_probe` without `--tests` runs only that binary.
   - `--exclude jackioh-tools` leaves every other member to the first leg.

Run from the repository root:
- `docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/repo" --workdir /repo rhysd/actionlint:1.7.7 -color .github/workflows/super.yml` passes.
- `cd bot/go && go test ./...` passes; `TestWorkflows_CIAndTheSuperRunWaitForTheRunnerGate` still counts 6 first jobs.
- Optional coverage proof. Each list is the leg's own command with `--list --format terse` added after `--ignored`:
  - `cargo test --workspace --tests --features jackioh-engine/testkit,jackioh-engine/ts -- --ignored --list --format terse | sort > all.txt`
  - The same for each of the three legs (the tools leg with its `--skip`), concatenated, `sort`ed, then `diff`ed against `all.txt`. The diff must be empty.

## Done when

- [ ] super.yml's header and `daily-tests` job read as in Steps 1–2.
- [ ] actionlint and `go test ./...` in `bot/go` pass.
- [ ] A dispatched super run on the branch shows `daily tests (every crate but the tools)`, `daily tests (tools)` and `daily tests (pool probe)` green, each under 60 minutes.
- [ ] `e2e (3/8)`: its log was read. Its failing test is named in the pull request, with an issue opened for it if it fails again.
- [ ] The pull request on `main` says which job each change makes pass and closes #4375.

## Risks

- **Coverage.** A leg selection that drops or repeats a test. The legs follow cargo's own package and target selection, and the optional list diff proves it.
- **Offline probe.** Without `cargo fetch`, the probe's nested `cargo test -p jackioh-server --offline` finds the server's crates missing on a fresh runner. The original single job fetched them through `--workspace`.
- **Cold caches.**
  - Each leg has its own `cache-key` (the setup action asks a matrix for that).
  - The first run of each key compiles from scratch, the probe's nested `target/pool-probe` included (about 10 minutes here).
  - Locally, every leg's tests plus a full compile stay well under 60 minutes: about 23, 18 and 25 minutes of tests.
- **Growth.**
  - When `FUZZ_POOL` passes 799 cards, `the_days_extra_seeds_keep_every_pool_card_s_deals_as_the_pool_grows` adds up to about 15 minutes to the tools leg (`DAILY_TOP_UP_MAX`, `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs`). That is still under 60.
  - A future slow test goes in whichever leg owns its crate.
- **Runner cost.** Three runners instead of one. The runner gate counts runs, not jobs.

  - Since `d5f68be`, main gained R4250000 (`c4bc8bd2a8`): a match or co-op socket's reconnect backoff starts over on its first view, not on open.
  - That was the one client change, and it is a candidate if the failure was a networked spec (20, 54, or 46's signed-in screens) meeting 429s.
  - If the log names a test that fails on its own assertion, it needs its own issue with that name.
- **Alternative rejected:** raising `timeout-minutes` to about 120. The work is serial and only grows with every new daily test, while the legs run in parallel and each keeps the 60-minute budget. A person may still prefer it.
````
